articles.title: ‘We miss her the same every day’: Olivia Cusack on her late footballer sister Maddy
articles.summary: Family is determined to ensure her ‘legacy lives on’ three years after the Sheffield United player’s death. Olivia Cusack says her sister, the late Maddy Cusack, is on her mind every single day and she is determined to ensure her “legacy lives on” three years after the former England youth…
body: Olivia, together with family and friends of Maddy, walked 29 miles from Bramall Lane, Sheffield United’s home, to their family’s home in Horsley, near Derby, on Saturday to raise funds and awareness. Maddy’s loved ones are still enduring a “frustrating and confusing” wait for answers about the circumstances surrounding her death on 20 September 2023.

An inquest into the death of the 27-year-old Sheffield United player was adjourned again in July and has been scheduled to resume on 7 December, after fresh evidence came to light. Cusack, a former England Under-19s international, was the first player to appear in 100 matches for Sheffield United’s women’s team.

Olivia says Saturday’s walk, “Bringing Maddy Home”, was motivated by some of the evidence the inquest heard. “After the inquest we wanted to bring her home from Bramall Lane, back to our family home,” she says. “Many people know Maddy as the professional football player and the name on the back of her shirt, the number, the colours she wore, the club she was associated with.

articles.title: Hayen must worry about his Burnley future but fans’ fears are existential
articles.summary: Derby’s stoppage-time equaliser leaves Burnley winless at home since last October and financial problems are mounting. The greatest moments of Burnley’s history were beamed on to a big screen before kick-off at Turf Moor, accompanied by famous lines of commentary.
body: Burnley appeared to have this game against Derby sewn up, leading through Zeki Amdouni’s first-half header, but a stunning stoppage-time strike from the Rams’ substitute Mohammed Fuseini soured the Turf Moor mood. It means Burnley’s winless home league run could now reach a year, the Clarets last tasting victory at Turf Moor on 18 October. Their last win in any competition in 90 minutes was on 11 February.

The draw left Nicky Hayen, the under-fire head coach, under scrutiny, though the majority of fans will direct their anger towards Alan Pace, the chair, given the financial problems and off-field turmoil that have plagued the club during a disruptive summer.

Hayen vowed to fight for his future and revealed he would talk with Pace, though could give no assurances he will remain in charge for the next game at Watford on 10 October after the extra-long international break. “I can understand the fans are angry after a start like this, it’s not what they want to see from their team or from myself,” he said. “It’s my responsibility. But I’ve always shown resilience and I’m always going to fight. We need this [international] window to change a lot of things.”

articles.title: Will the three-week break put more pressure on managers?
articles.summary: So far this season three coaches have lost their jobs, but plenty of others will be looking over their shoulders heading into the new, extended international break.
body: Three weeks is a long time in football - especially if you are a manager struggling for results.
So far this season three coaches have lost their jobs - Paul Heckingbottom at Preston North End, Michael Duff at Wycombe Wanderers and Peterborough's Luke Williams.
That includes the managers of Fulham and Manchester United, who on Sunday meet at Craven Cottage in the final fixture before players jet off around the world with their countries.
It will all be pretty new to Alvaro Arbeloa, appointed as Fulham's manager in the summer after taking charge of just 28 games as Real Madrid boss in the second half of last season.

articles.title: Mourinho and Simeone renew rivalry in Madrid derby after more than a decade
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho and Diego Simeone renew their rivalry after a 12-year wait as Real Madrid visit Atletico Madrid in Sunday's Spanish capital derby.
body: When Atletico Madrid welcome Real Madrid to Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday, Jose Mourinho and Diego Simeone will renew a rivalry not seen for more than a decade.
The two managers have not faced each other since 2014, when Mourinho was manager of Chelsea and Atleti knocked the English side out of the Champions League at Stamford Bridge.
But this will not be their first Madrid derby as rival managers.

That came two years before the Champions League encounter, when Simeone's Atletico welcomed Mourinho to their former home, the Vicente Calderon Stadium, during the Portuguese's first reign as Real boss - he left with a 4-1 win that day.

articles.title: Golden Nuggets: Game day
articles.summary: I can’t wait to see how Connor Colby and Jake Brendel handle the Miami Dolphins defensive line, how the 49ers secondary takes care of the Dolphins offense, and whether the 49ers throttle up or down.
body: How the 49ers are readjusting after weeklong Australia trip “Perry, the team’s vice president of player health and performance, and his staff provided players with instructions on how much water to drink on the plane, how long to stay up before falling asleep and when to wake up.

Right tackle Colton McKivitz said the objective was to stay up for a couple of hours (an easy enough task with so much adrenaline still pumping from the game), go to sleep in their lie-flat seats, and then wake up for the final few hours of the flight.

McKivitz estimated he slept for about seven hours. Running back Christian McCaffrey said he was out for about 13 hours, which was about the same as rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton. Defensive end Nick Bosa was in the same range.

“I actually felt it worse on the way back,” Bosa said. “Going out, you just kind of power through a few hours and then go to bed early and then just stay on a little earlier wake-up is what I did. And then when I came back, it’s been kind of hard to get to bed, but [Tuesday] night I got to bed nice and early.”

articles.title: Colwill's 'surreal' Ronaldo and Haaland ambition
articles.summary: In just 12 months, the Cardiff City midfielder has gone from League One football to the prospect of facing Cristiano Ronaldo and Erling Haaland.
body: Roll the clock back 12 months and Joel Colwill was facing then uncapped Icelandic midfielder Benony Breki Andresson, as Cardiff City drew 1-1 at Stockport in League One.
One year on, and the 21-year-old Welsh youngster is hoping to share the pitch with Portuguese great Cristiano Ronaldo and Norwegian goal-machine Erling Haaland.

Colwill has been included in Craig Bellamy's 28-man squad for Wales upcoming Nations League A campaign against Portugal, Norway and Denmark, and the Cardiff midfielder cannot quite believe he could be facing footballing legends.
"Hopefully if I get the opportunity to play against both of those players, it'll be pretty surreal, especially Ronaldo, one of the greatest players of all time," said Colwill.

articles.title: Denis Zakaria on Monaco teammate Lamine Camara: ‘Chelsea? I told him that it was good but that it’s better here.’
articles.summary: Lamine Camara’s prospective move to Chelsea broke down on transfer deadline day. The Senegal international remained at AS Monaco, who pulled the plug on the deal at the final hour.
body: Camara has since said that he has “turned the page”, despite the Principality club’s CEO admitting that the midfielder had come to him, asking him to facilitate a move. To refocus, Camara said that he spoke with many teammates, including Zakaria, who once played at Chelsea during a season on loan. “Chelsea? I told him that it was good but that it is better here,” the Switzerland international joked in a mixed zone interview attended by Get French Football News.

Speaking after Friday night’s win over RC Lens (2-1), Zakaria continued, “I know the player and the person that he is; he is very professional. I think that [the transfer saga] has given him even more strength. He was incredible today.”

articles.title: Brown delivers Hatton tribute after winning British and Commonwealth titles
articles.summary: Pat Brown won the vacant British and Commonwealth cruiserweight titles on home turf on Saturday night, counting out John Hedges in the sixth round at Co-op Live with a body shot he dedicated to Ricky Hatton.
body: The 26-year-old Olympian took his professional record to seven wins from seven, every one inside the distance, adding the Lonsdale Belt to the WBA International and IBF Intercontinental titles already in his possession.
For Hedges, it was a case of unlucky number 13 after the Harlow-born fighter had gone unbeaten through his first 12 fights.

It was anything but straightforward for Brown, though. Hedges is 6ft 6in, and a southpaw, and the 24-year-old spent the opening exchanges making himself hard to hit, giving Brown nothing to aim at and grabbing hold whenever the Mancunian worked his way inside.
Frustration began to build for Brown and he started leaning on Hedges with his head and forcing him back over the top rope until referee Reece Carter intervened.

articles.title: Jose Mourinho needs to help Real Madrid overcome their Metropolitano curse: Opinion
articles.summary: Real Madrid are one of Spain’s historic giants, and the consequence of being around for as long as they have is the inevitable rivalries that appear over time. There are stadiums around Spain where Los Blancos expect hostility.
body: Madrid head into today’s derby against Atletico having won only one of their last seven La Liga visits to the Metropolitano.
That solitary victory came back in September 2022. It is an uncomfortable record for a club that normally prides itself on travelling anywhere without changing its expectations.
Atletico are strong at home, the atmosphere is hostile and Diego Simeone’s teams know exactly how to turn these games into physical, emotional contests.
A one-off loss to them can be explained away. Seven league visits begin to tell a different story about Madrid, though.

body: In June, Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson were suspended from the second Test of the 2-1 series loss to New Zealand due to a nightclub incident that occurred in the wake of their opening win at Lord's.

Last month, Brydon Carse was handcuffed outside a nightclub in Derby and missed the second and third Tests of England's series whitewash of Pakistan, prompting Test captain Joe Root to describe himself as "hacked off" by the growing list of alcohol-related incidents involving England players.
"It's disappointing," Fleming said. "The way that players represent England and the group is going to be really important to me."
He added: "I watched Joe in the press conference, and when he voices his displeasure at the behaviour, I think that said it all.

articles.title: McIlroy two off Wentworth lead and ready to 'play aggressively'
articles.summary: Manuel Elvira and Filippo Celli share the lead heading into the final round of the BMW PGA Championship after they both made birdies on the 18th to move one ahead at Wentworth.
body: Rather remarkably, 20 players will go into Sunday within four shots of the lead, including Rory McIlroy, who produced a box-office finish, sending the patrons into delirium on the 18th by making an eagle to move within two shots of the pace-setting duo at 11 under par.
McIlroy equalled four other players - Adam Scott, Joaquin Niemann, Davis Bryant and Kristoffer Reitan - to finish tied for sixth on the leaderboard through 54 holes.
In windy conditions, Spain's Alejandro Del Rey and American duo Johannes Veerman and JJ Spaun had all been tied with Celli and Elvira at 12 under par late in the third round.
Del Rey and Veerman had enjoyed epic days on the course, each shooting low scores of eight-under 64 to shoot up the leaderboard.
